text: Keep `android:appCategory="game"` in the Android manifest, or drop it?
context:
BRL-gv67 is confirmed on the Pixel 8a (details in the spec). With the category, Play Services starts a game session (`GameService … createGameSession`). Its invisible `Embedded{}` overlay takes window focus on the first tap in the first ~2.4 s after a cold launch, so 6 of 6 taps at 1.8–2.2 s were lost. Without the category, all of those taps reached the app.

The category also turns on things beyond the overlay: Android's Game Dashboard and Play Games entry for the app, `GameManagerService` "Game power mode ON" while in the foreground, and a default 60 FPS frame-rate override. Our own `ANativeWindow_setFrameRate(60)` vote (`packages/brawler-android/src/frame_pacing.rs`) already sets 60 FPS. Play Store categorization does not come from this attribute: the store category is set in the Play Console listing. `appCategory` is the on-device hint used by Game Dashboard, Digital Wellbeing and battery/game-mode policy. The deprecated `android:isGame` is only for pre-API-26 devices; our minSdk is 31.

suggestions.detail: No change. Players keep Game Dashboard (recording, FPS, Do Not Disturb), Android game power mode and Game Mode policy. The cost is that a tap in roughly the first 2.4 s after a cold launch can be swallowed. Real players rarely tap that early, because Select Server or the Dashboard is still appearing.

Remove `android:appCategory="game"` from `packages/brawler-android/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`. Early taps always reach the app. The app loses Game Dashboard, Android game power mode and the Game Mode frame-rate override. The device may also list it as a regular app in the Games / Digital Wellbeing categories. Play Store placement is unaffected, because the Console listing sets it.
